# Godot reuse-first creation acceptance

1. In a native PI Godot fixture, request a new playable object. The first offered tool set contains the host's exact godot_source_library schema. Its initial search call goes through ordinary tools.execute without ToolSearch. Unregistered, legacy, summary, review and finished-task cases retain exclusions.
2. Read an immutable archive containing a helper dependency. Require the exact internal id/version/sha256 relation to the returned resource, empty leaf dependencies, unchanged catalog archiveRef, no source bodies and no installation. Existing corruption, wrong hash, stale source, lost reply, group identity and authorization regressions must still pass.
3. Load the authoring guidance catalog and page the generated library/asset-index.json reference with exact version/hash and source pins. Catalog responses must not contain the index body. Reject wrong hashes and source changes. Reference-world rows must not be presented as installable components or a new source-reading capability; historical interface reference hashes and cohorts stay unchanged.
4. Check the guidance distinguishes static meshes from behavior, automatic nodes from manual helper wiring, current full-auto installation from player-confirmed proposals, and checks/application from actual gameplay.
5. In the next separate real-player run, ask for a sword and a pursuing monster without naming a package. Observe targeted discovery/read, compatible assembly, real input/damage and saved/cold-restored behavior. For an unmatched idea, require continued original creation without exhaustive library search or reduced gameplay. These model-behavior claims require that real run; pure fixtures only establish the offered tools and contracts.

Targeted entry points: craftmine-context.test.ts; tests/godot-final-install-assets/source-library.test.mjs; tests/source-library-read-hints.test.mjs; tests/creation-guidance/*.test.mjs; scripts/refresh-guidance-cohorts.mjs --check. No native engine, model or active player profile is needed for these contract checks.
